argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Explicitly stated and repeatedly clarified through distinctions

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High: engages with strongest objections and distinguishes senses of key terms
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High: each distinction bears directly on the validity of the reductio
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Mixed: mathematical premises are standard, but metaphysical premises are contested

distinctions_drawn: logical vs. physical vs. practical impossibility
infinite series as a whole vs. infinite process
beginningless sequence vs. completed infinite task
explicit_definitions_given: actual infinite: a completed totality containing infinitely many members
potential infinite: an unending process always capable of further extension
Principle of Correspondence: a set is infinite iff it can be put into one-to-one correspondence with a proper subset of itself
absurdity: formal contradiction, logical incoherence, metaphysical impossibility, physical impossibility, practical impossibility, or psychological unintelligibility

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Distinguishes between mathematical consistency and metaphysical instantiation; accepts that concrete infinities may be physically impossible while denying logical impossibility
objections_raised: An infinite library could never be acquired by successive addition
The present could not be reached after an infinite past
Concrete infinities are impossible because they involve causal/material dependence
LDS beginninglessness is ruled out by successive addition

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis, mathematical examples, theological doctrine, philosophical distinctions

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Analytic metaphysics of time and modality
philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Neutral-critical: defends LDS eternalism against Craig's reductio while acknowledging the force of Craig's challenges
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Actual infinity, beginningless time, successive addition, LDS eternalism, limits of reductio arguments

structural_organization.structure_type: Dialectical: thesis, clarification, objections, replies, application, final assessment

summary_of_core_decisions: The text argues that Craig's reductio arguments against actual infinity are challenges, not demonstrations. They show that infinity is counter-intuitive and that concrete infinities may be physically or metaphysically problematic, but they do not establish formal contradiction. LDS theology can consistently affirm beginningless time or eternal matter if it distinguishes mathematical infinity from concrete instantiation and provides an account of causal/temporal grounding.

thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: High: 'can therefore consistently accommodate', 'provided it distinguishes', 'may be defensible', 'not refuted'
